natural: Dusting off their hats and congratulating each other

meaning.en: To gloat together at the prospect of office or gain (derogatory).
meaning.zh: 指官场中一人当了官或升了官，其同伙也互相庆贺将有官可做。多用于贬义。

examples.zh: 对手下台，这伙人弹冠相庆。
examples.en: When their rival fell, the clique gloated together.

examples.zh: 别高兴太早，现在还不是弹冠相庆的时候。
examples.en: Don't celebrate yet — it's too early to gloat.

story.en: Wang Ji and Gong Yu were close friends; it was said "when Wang Yang is in office, Gong dusts off his cap" — expecting to be recommended in turn.
story.zh: 王吉与贡禹是好友，时人说："王阳在位，贡公弹冠。"意思是王吉做了官，贡禹也准备出来做官。

natural: A clear heart with few desires

meaning.en: To keep a tranquil mind and few desires.
meaning.zh: 保持心地清净，减少欲望。

examples.zh: 他退休后清心寡欲，每天读书种花。
examples.en: In retirement he lives simply, reading and gardening every day.

examples.zh: 清心寡欲有益于健康。
examples.en: A tranquil mind with few desires is good for health.

natural: A rat's eyes see only an inch

meaning.en: Short-sighted; lacking vision.
meaning.zh: 形容目光短浅，没有远见。

equivalents: can't see beyond the end of one's nose

examples.zh: 只看眼前利益是鼠目寸光。
examples.en: Focusing only on immediate gain is short-sighted.

examples.zh: 他鼠目寸光，错过了大好机会。
examples.en: Being short-sighted, he missed a golden opportunity.

antonyms: 不畏浮云遮望眼，自缘身在最高层

natural: Not crossing the Lei Pool

meaning.en: Not to overstep a set limit.
meaning.zh: 比喻不敢超越一定的范围和界限。

examples.zh: 他做事谨慎，从不越雷池一步。
examples.en: He's cautious and never oversteps the mark.

examples.zh: 他工作多年始终不越雷池，严守财务纪律。
examples.en: In all his years at work he has never overstepped the line on financial rules.

story.en: When rebels attacked the capital, Yu Liang wrote to the general Wen Jiao: "Do not cross the Lei Pool by a single step" (足下无过雷池一步) — telling him to hold his post rather than come to the capital.
story.zh: 庾亮给温峤写信："足下无过雷池一步也。"让他坚守原防地。

natural: Clinging to life and fearing death

meaning.en: Cowardly; clinging to life.
meaning.zh: 贪恋生存，畏惧死亡。指为了活命而丧失气节。

examples.zh: 在敌人面前，他贪生怕死，当了叛徒。
examples.en: Faced with the enemy, he saved his own skin and became a traitor.

examples.zh: 军人决不能贪生怕死。
examples.en: A soldier must never be a coward.

antonyms: 拼将十万头颅血，须把乾坤力挽回
一寸山河一寸血，十万青年十万军
千锤万凿出深山，烈火焚烧若等闲
苟利国家生死以，岂因祸福避趋之
人生自古谁无死，留取丹心照汗青
生当作人杰，死亦为鬼雄
生，亦我所欲也；义，亦我所欲也；二者不可得兼，舍生而取义者也
寄意寒星荃不察，我以我血荐轩辕
男儿何不带吴钩，收取关山五十州
我自横刀向天笑，去留肝胆两昆仑
至今思项羽，不肯过江东
捐躯赴国难，视死忽如归

natural: Cook Ding carving the ox

meaning.en: Consummate skill from understanding a thing's nature.
meaning.zh: 比喻经过反复实践，掌握了事物的客观规律，做事得心应手。

examples.zh: 他处理这类问题如庖丁解牛，游刃有余。
examples.en: He handles such problems with consummate ease.

examples.zh: 学习要有庖丁解牛的精神，摸清规律。
examples.en: Learn like Cook Ding — understand how things really work.

story.en: Cook Ding carved an ox for Lord Wenhui with such grace it was like a dance. He explained he no longer saw the whole ox, only the natural gaps between joints; his knife had stayed sharp for nineteen years.
story.zh: 庖丁为文惠君宰牛，动作合乎音乐节拍。他说自己"目无全牛"，依照牛的自然结构下刀，刀用了十九年还像新的一样。

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

natural: Nodding and bowing

meaning.en: To bow and scrape; obsequious.
meaning.zh: 形容恭顺或过分客气，带有讨好的意味。

examples.zh: 他见了领导就点头哈腰。
examples.en: He bows and scrapes whenever he sees the boss.

examples.zh: 做生意要有原则，不必点头哈腰。
examples.en: Do business with principles — no need to grovel.

usage.zh: 多作谓语、状语，口语，贬义。

natural: Nüwa mending the sky

meaning.en: A heroic effort to repair a disaster.
meaning.zh: 古代神话。比喻改造天地的雄伟气魄和斗争精神。

examples.zh: 女娲补天是中国著名的神话故事。
examples.en: Nüwa mending the sky is a famous Chinese myth.

examples.zh: 治理这片沙漠，需要女娲补天的精神。
examples.en: Reclaiming this desert will take a Herculean effort.

story.en: When the pillars of heaven broke, the goddess Nüwa melted five-coloured stones to patch the sky and cut off a giant turtle's legs to prop it up, saving humanity.
story.zh: 远古天柱折断，天塌地陷，女娲炼五色石补天，斩鳌足立四极，拯救了人类。

natural: Treasuring ink like gold

meaning.en: Sparing with words or brushstrokes; concise.
meaning.zh: 爱惜墨就像金子一样。指不轻易动笔，作画、写文章力求精练。

examples.zh: 这位画家惜墨如金，寥寥几笔就画出了神韵。
examples.en: Sparing with his brush, the painter captured the essence in a few strokes.

examples.zh: 写作要惜墨如金，不说废话。
examples.en: Be economical with words — no padding.

natural: Drawing a tiger by copying a cat

meaning.en: To copy mechanically; imitate superficially.
meaning.zh: 比喻照着样子模仿。

examples.zh: 刚开始学做菜，只能照猫画虎。
examples.en: When you start cooking, you just copy recipes mechanically.

examples.zh: 照猫画虎地抄作业是学不到东西的。
examples.en: Copying homework without understanding teaches you nothing.

synonyms: 照葫芦画瓢——按老样子做

natural: Time flies like an arrow

meaning.en: Time flies.
meaning.zh: 时间像箭一样飞逝。形容时间过得极快。

examples.zh: 光阴似箭，日月如梭。
examples.en: Time flies like an arrow; the days and months like a shuttle.

examples.zh: 光阴似箭，转眼孩子已经上大学了。
examples.en: Time flies — the children are already at university.

usage.en: Usually an opening clause. Very common in school writing.

natural: Mountain upon mountain, river upon river

meaning.en: Seemingly endless obstacles; a winding, confusing way.
meaning.zh: 一座座山、一道道水重重叠叠。也比喻困难重重。

examples.zh: 山重水复疑无路，柳暗花明又一村。
examples.en: Mountains and rivers everywhere — no way through, it seems; then willows and flowers, and another village.

examples.zh: 研究陷入山重水复的困境。
examples.en: The research ran into obstacle after obstacle.

story.en: Lu You's couplet: "Mountains and rivers layer on layer — I doubt there's a way; shady willows and bright flowers — another village appears."
story.zh: 陆游《游山西村》："山重水复疑无路，柳暗花明又一村。"

usage.en: Usually in the couplet with 柳暗花明. 重 is chóng.
usage.zh: 常与"柳暗花明"连用。"重"读 chóng。

natural: Bullying the soft and fearing the hard

meaning.en: To bully the weak and fear the strong.
meaning.zh: 欺负软弱的，害怕强硬的。

examples.zh: 他欺软怕硬，见了强者就低头。
examples.en: He's a bully and a coward — he grovels to the strong.

examples.zh: 欺软怕硬的人最让人看不起。
examples.en: People who bully the weak are the most despicable.

synonyms: 雷公打豆腐——专拣软的欺
黄鼠狼单咬病鸭子——专拣弱的欺
老太太吃柿子——专挑软的捏
antonyms: 横眉冷对千夫指，俯首甘为孺子牛

natural: Crane-white hair and a child's face

meaning.en: White-haired but rosy-cheeked; healthy in old age.
meaning.zh: 白色的头发，红润的面色。形容老年人气色好，精神旺盛。

examples.zh: 这位老人鹤发童颜，精神矍铄。
examples.en: The old man is silver-haired but hale and hearty.

examples.zh: 九十岁的奶奶依然鹤发童颜。
examples.en: At ninety, Grandma is still youthful-looking and healthy.

usage.en: Predicate or attributive. 发 is fà (hair).
usage.zh: 多作谓语、定语。"发"读 fà。

natural: As clear as watching a fire

meaning.en: To see things with perfect clarity.
meaning.zh: 形容观察事物非常清楚，好像看火一样。

examples.zh: 他对市场形势洞若观火。
examples.en: He has a crystal-clear view of the market situation.

examples.zh: 对方的意图，他洞若观火。
examples.en: He saw right through the other side's intentions.

story.en: King Pangeng told his officials: "I see it as clearly as watching a fire" (予若观火).

date.zh: 西周至战国 · 前11—前3世纪
date.en: Western Zhou to Warring States, 11th–3rd c. BC

natural: Deciding once who is hen and who is cock

meaning.en: To fight it out to see who is stronger; a showdown.
meaning.zh: 比喻较量一下，决定胜负高低。

equivalents: settle it once and for all

examples.zh: 两支球队将在决赛中一决雌雄。
examples.en: The two teams will go head to head in the final.

examples.zh: 他们约定明天一决雌雄。
examples.en: They agreed to settle it once and for all tomorrow.

story.en: Xiang Yu proposed to Liu Bang: "Let us two challenge each other and decide who is hen and who is cock" (愿与汉王挑战决雌雄), sparing the people.
story.zh: 项羽对刘邦说："愿与汉王挑战决雌雄，毋徒苦天下之民父子为也。"

usage.en: Predicate. In speech 一 is yì.

natural: Plant melons and you get melons

meaning.en: You reap what you sow.
meaning.zh: 种什么就收获什么。比喻做了什么样的事，就会得到什么样的结果。

equivalents: as you sow, so shall you reap

examples.zh: 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆。
examples.en: Plant melons and you get melons; plant beans and you get beans.

examples.zh: 平时努力，考试自然好，种瓜得瓜嘛。
examples.en: Work hard and you'll do well in exams — you reap what you sow.

usage.en: Usually 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆. 种 is zhòng (to plant).
usage.zh: 常说"种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆"。"种"读 zhòng。

natural: Rare birds and exotic beasts

meaning.en: Rare birds and animals.
meaning.zh: 珍贵稀有的鸟兽。

examples.zh: 这片原始森林里生活着许多珍禽异兽。
examples.en: Much rare wildlife lives in this primeval forest.

examples.zh: 动物园里有很多珍禽异兽。
examples.en: The zoo has many exotic animals.

usage.en: Subject or object. A descriptive 四字词语.

natural: Climbing a tree to look for fish

meaning.en: To use the wrong method; a futile approach.
meaning.zh: 爬到树上去找鱼。比喻方向或办法不对，不可能达到目的。

equivalents: look for a needle in the wrong haystack

examples.zh: 靠打游戏提高成绩，无异于缘木求鱼。
examples.en: Trying to improve your grades by gaming is barking up the wrong tree.

examples.zh: 用错误的方法解决问题，是缘木求鱼。
examples.en: Using the wrong method is a futile approach.

story.en: Mencius told King Xuan of Qi that seeking to dominate the world by force was "like climbing a tree to look for fish".
story.zh: 孟子对齐宣王说："以若所为，求若所欲，犹缘木而求鱼也。"

natural: Never letting the book out of one's hand

meaning.en: Always reading; never without a book.
meaning.zh: 书本不离手。形容勤奋好学。

equivalents: always has their nose in a book

examples.zh: 爷爷八十多岁了，仍然手不释卷。
examples.en: Grandpa is over eighty and still always has his nose in a book.

examples.zh: 她手不释卷，知识非常渊博。
examples.en: She's an avid reader and very knowledgeable.

origin.source: 《三国志·吴书·吕蒙传》裴松之注引《江表传》

story.en: Sun Quan urged the general Lü Meng to study, saying that Emperor Guangwu, even amid the pressures of war, "never let the book out of his hand" (手不释卷). The passage is quoted by Pei Songzhi from Yu Pu's Jiangbiao Zhuan.
story.zh: 孙权劝吕蒙读书，说光武帝在军务繁忙时仍“手不释卷”。此段为裴松之注引虞溥《江表传》。

natural: Stealing a mean existence

meaning.en: To cling to life without dignity.
meaning.zh: 得过且过，苟且贪生。

examples.zh: 他宁死也不愿苟且偷生。
examples.en: He'd rather die than cling to life without dignity.

examples.zh: 亡国之后，有人苟且偷生，有人奋起反抗。
examples.en: After the fall, some clung to life while others rose up.

antonyms: 生当作人杰，死亦为鬼雄
生，亦我所欲也；义，亦我所欲也；二者不可得兼，舍生而取义者也
至今思项羽，不肯过江东

natural: A heart like a monkey, a mind like a horse

meaning.en: Restless and distracted; unable to concentrate.
meaning.zh: 心像猴子跳，意像马在跑。形容心思不定，变化无常。

examples.zh: 快放假了，同学们都心猿意马。
examples.en: With the holidays near, the students can't concentrate.

examples.zh: 他上课心猿意马，什么也没听进去。
examples.en: His mind was all over the place in class, and nothing sank in.

usage.en: Predicate. From Buddhist imagery of the restless mind.

natural: The lion's roar from Hedong

meaning.en: A shrewish wife scolding her husband (humorous).
meaning.zh: 比喻悍妇发怒，并借以嘲笑惧内的人。

examples.zh: 他怕老婆，一听河东狮吼就乖乖回家了。
examples.en: He's henpecked — at the first roar from his wife he heads straight home.

examples.zh: 朋友们常拿他的河东狮吼开玩笑。
examples.en: His friends often joke about his formidable wife.

origin.source: 苏轼《寄吴德仁兼简陈季常》

story.en: Su Shi teased his friend Chen Jichang, whose wife Liu (from Hedong) was fierce: "Suddenly hearing the lion's roar from Hedong, his staff falls from his hand and his mind goes blank."
story.zh: 苏轼戏陈季常："忽闻河东狮子吼，拄杖落手心茫然。"陈妻柳氏是河东人，性凶悍。

usage.en: Subject or object. Humorous; can sound sexist, so use with care.
usage.zh: 多作主语、宾语，诙谐用语。

natural: Diligence can make up for clumsiness

meaning.en: Hard work makes up for lack of talent.
meaning.zh: 勤奋能够弥补不足。

equivalents: practice makes up for lack of talent

examples.zh: 我不聪明，但勤能补拙。
examples.en: I'm not clever, but hard work makes up for it.

examples.zh: 勤能补拙是良训。
examples.en: Hard work making up for talent is good advice.

synonyms: 书山有路勤为径，学海无涯苦作舟

natural: Broken copper and rusty iron

meaning.en: Scrap metal; worthless junk.
meaning.zh: 指废旧金属器物。也比喻没有用的东西。

examples.zh: 他把家里的破铜烂铁都卖了。
examples.en: He sold all the scrap metal from the house.

examples.zh: 这台旧机器已经成了破铜烂铁。
examples.en: The old machine is now just a pile of junk.
